To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the DLHL DDR structures are superior to other structures in the sense that they exhibit much higher negative resistance and higher efficiency.

DLHL DDR IMPATTS exhibit much higher negative conductivity than flat and SLHL devices and that the height of the first bumps and the active region width have a strong influence on the small-signal properties of the DLHL devices.

the double low - high - high - low (DLHL) structure is the most efficient structure for high-current-density operation, and that the DLHL structure with rectangular-shaped bumps gives better performance than the structure with trapezoidal-shaped bumps, although the former is not easy to fabricate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of high-power silicon IMPATT diode structures for operation around 95 GHz.
the optimization of the structural parameters of the DLHL structure, so as to improve the performance of the device at high current densities.

a detailed investigation of the high-frequency properties and the small-signal performance of pulsed-mode silicon IMPATTs at high current densities, and the results obtained are of practical significance in the design and development of pulsed-mode mm-wave silicon IMPATTs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DLHL DDR structure is a very promising candidate for high-power pulsed operation in the mm-wave frequency range.

the DLHL structure, with trapezoidal bumps, is the most suitable for operation at high current density, and that the width of active region is a critical factor for the design of the DLHL IMPATT diode.
the DLHL DDR silicon IMPATT device with optimized parameters is the best structure for high power generation at high current density.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a low - high - high structure is more suitable for high-power generation in pulsed IMPATT diodes than a low - high – low structure.
the DLHL DDR structure, when optimized for high-frequency operation, is a promising structure for high-power pulsed operation at mm-wave frequencies.
the DLHL IMPATT diodes have the potential to generate higher power at 94 GHz and higher frequencies, and the results presented in the paper would be useful for designing such devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that

DLHL structure is the best structure to achieve high-power generation in the DDR IMPATT devices at high current densities and that the height of the first bumps plays a vital role in determining the high-frequency properties and the power generation capability of these devices.
the DLHL IMPATT diode can produce a negative conductance of 0.5 S at a current density as high as 2 kA/cm ^{2}, and can be operated as a pulsed oscillator at 94 GHz.
a low - high - high - low (LHHHL) structure is more suitable for high current density operation.
